entries.description: Register.

Delete the inferred import graph and everything that serves it: `PACKAGE`, `module_name_for`, `_imports_in`, `build_import_graph`, `_closure`, `build_test_dependencies`, and the `dependency-edge` and `module-ownership` reasons. The reasons that remain — `changed-test`, `configured-rule`, `repo_wide`, and smoke on `selection_unknown` — carry no language knowledge.

Replace `test_*.py` discovery with declared test roots and a declared test-file glob, so a repository states where its tests live and what they are called instead of the framework guessing a pytest convention.

Declare this repository's own mapping under `testing.selection.rules`, covering what the graph used to infer. Rules are the honest form of a mapping that was always a guess; where a module genuinely affects many suites, say so.
Affected tests, recorded as the `preverify-targeted` evidence.
Cross-provider verification; then the full suite once, against the final verified tree.
Close-out.
Registered session 1 (copilot).
Register.

Deleted the AST import graph from affected.py: PACKAGE, module_name_for, _imports_in, build_import_graph, _closure, build_test_dependencies, test_files, and the module-ownership and dependency-edge reasons. Remaining reasons carry no language knowledge.
Replaced tree discovery of test_*.py with declared testing.selection.test_roots plus a declared test_glob, matched case-sensitively against the file name and confirmed present in the tree.
Declared one testing.selection rule per ai_router module, naming the tests that would notice it breaking, replacing what the import graph inferred.
Ran the selector's targeted command (103 tests, green) and recorded it as preverify-targeted evidence; accepted under the targeted policy.

Round 1 ISSUES_FOUND (evidence.py and ledger.py rules omitted tests/test_critique_contracts.py, which imports both); remediated, reran the fix's targeted tests, round 2 VERIFIED by gpt-5.5/openai over copilot-cli.
Complete suite green (476) against the final verified tree and recorded as final-full; work committed and pushed; closing through the gate.
Register.

Replace AST-chain quote provenance with digest-pinned line-range provenance: the reviewed tree's digest, the exact line range, and a byte-exact match of the quoted text. That triple is what makes a quote checkable; the enclosing node chain was a refinement available in one language.

Delete `PARSED_SUFFIXES` and the `ast.parse` call sites over reviewed source, so a quote from a `.cs`, `.java`, `.ts` or `.sql` file is checked exactly as rigorously as one from a `.py` file. Today it is refused.

State the residual honestly in the check vocabulary: line-range provenance proves *where a quote came from*, not *what kind of construct it is*. A check that needs the difference is a check for a deterministic analyzer, which the control surface already routes.
Affected tests, recorded as the `preverify-targeted` evidence.
Cross-provider verification; then the full suite once, against the final verified tree.
Close-out.
Registered session 2 (copilot).
Simplified verify_quote to path/content_hash/span only (digest-pinned line-range provenance); removed ast_kind and required_kinds. Updated worker-results.schema.json to drop ast_kind.

Deleted PARSED_SUFFIXES, ast_kinds_at, _count_ast_matches, _node_dotted_name, contract_ast_kinds, and all ast.parse call sites in evidence.py; ABSENCE_QUERY_KINDS is now (literal, regex). A quote from any file the tree contains is now checked identically.

verify_quote and the provenance section docstring now state the residual: a quote proves where its text came from, never what construct it is; a check needing that difference routes to a deterministic analyzer (g0-deterministic executor). Updated the checks.json/widget.py fixture to drop the Kind:dotted.name AST vocabulary in favour of plain text existence/count.
Selector printed 7 files (157 tests); ran the exact command, all passed; recorded as preverify-targeted, policy targeted.

Round 1/2 ISSUES_FOUND (pass-on-forbidden-literal in the seeded fixture); remediated by recording result:fail for the matches:2 case and made the narrower-check demo internally consistent (subprocess.run( literal absent -> pass). Round 2's residual demand for a code-level condition/branch evaluator was disputed as out of session 2's scope (critique artifacts decide nothing yet per test_critique_contracts.py:4 and STATUS.md:110-119; that belongs to 144/145). Round 3 VERIFIED by gpt-5.5/openai over copilot-cli, dispute withdrawn.
